result.title: When Does Dynamics Randomization Test Context Inference?
result.summary: Environments with randomized dynamics are widely used to ask whether world models need explicit context inference. However, randomization can leave little predictive information for a context encoder to add, because distinct latent parameters may produce similar transitions at visited states, or those states may already reveal the active context. We formalize the remaining one-step information as predictive headroom and compare kernels under fixed and visited state--action distributions to distinguish changes in query coverage from changes in context weights. We analyze discrete and continuous environments and find low headroom both when kernels differ little and when visitation reduces an otherwise large discrepancy. At the same time, resetting state components increases headroom, showing that context evidence accumulates in state. We propose reporting this headroom alongside the randomized parameters, so that gains from explicit context inference can be interpreted relative to the information missing from the current state and action.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将随机动力学环境下 context encoder 能额外提供的一步预测信息形式化为 predictive headroom，并在固定与访问状态—动作分布下比较转移核，以区分查询覆盖变化与 context 权重变化；分析显示 headroom 在多种情形下偏低，而重置状态分量会使其升高。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「当前状态已包含多少证据、还缺多少」的量化框架可能可供核查迁移到 LVR 诊断：判断 latent 状态相对观测是否带来额外可用信息，并区分信息缺失与根本没被查询到，与贡献分配和证据累积问题相关。
